Some characteristics of this plane were ascribed to the [[World Tree cosmology]] planes of [[Green Fields]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn}} and the [[House of the Triad]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn}} when that cosmology became popular. In the [[World Axis cosmology]], Celestia was interpreted as an [[astral dominion]] ruled over by [[Torm]] as it drifted through the [[Astral Sea]].{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|62}} {{Quote |A cutter who comes to Mount Celestia for easy answers to his troubles is, well... He's clueless. Good and law may be lots of things, but they ain't easy. |A paladin of the [[Order of the Eternal Sun]]{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Mount Celestia|2}} }} ==Description== Celestia was the ultimate in law and good. All aspects of Celestia were beautiful and perfect; it was where the souls of many creatures of lawful good alignment went to after death.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|89}} Celestia was home to numerous celestial creatures including various types of [[Celestial archon|archons]], the [[petitioner]]s of this plane. As an outer plane, Celestia was spatially infinite and consisted of seven infinite layers (or sub-planes). The seven individual layers formed a colossal mountain that rose from an infinite sea of holy water on the bottommost layer, to the summit on the topmost layer. Ascending the mountain was analogous to travelling through subsequently higher or 'deeper' layers to the top. Each of the seven layers contained at least one mountain or high structure rising into the sky, and most had whole mountain ranges. The barriers between the seven layers were arranged such that entrances were at the lowest geographical points and exits were at the highest, so a traveler from the [[Astral Plane]] would enter the first layer at the base of a mountain (actually, in the surf of the ocean surrounding the mountain) and had to climb to the peak to reach the next layer, only to emerge at the nadir again. The sky of each layer had its own hue which softly bathed everything in gentle shades of luminance. ===Lunia=== {{/Imagemap}} {{Main|Lunia}} Celestia's first (bottommost) layer shared borders with the neighboring planes of the [[Arcadia|Peaceable Kingdoms of Arcadia]] and the [[Bytopia|Twin Paradises of Bytopia]]; travel was possible between Celestia and these planes at certain locations. Known as the Silver Heaven, Lunia was the first layer travelers encountered. The sky of Lunia was a nighttime sky filled with stars that illuminated the layer with a [[silver]] glow. The ''color pools'' of the Astral Plane would deposit visitors in the surf of a vast ocean, the Silver Sea,{{Cite book/Stormwrack|10}} full of clean, fresh water that had the properties of ''[[holy water]]''. The sky above Lunia was perpetually dark, filled with beautiful constellations of silver stars bright enough to illuminate the base of the mountain. The dark, starry Silver Sea was full of many good aquatic beings, including [[Celestial creature|celestial]] [[whale]]s and [[sea elves]]. The adjacent beach belonged to an island with a majestic mountain decorated with grand citadels made from polished white stone. Descriptions of the citadels varied among travelers leading cosmologists to theorize that there were many of these mountain islands. Also in the surf of Lunia were the portals to the [[Twin Paradises]], [[Arcadia]], and [[Concordant Opposition]] which were large, permanent, free-standing blocks of finished stone. Black [[granite]] blocks veined with gold led to Arcadia, white granite blocks with veins of silver led to the Twin Paradises, and red granite blocks flecked with blue took you to Concordant Opposition. Travelers merely had to touch a block to activate the portal. [[File:Lunia.jpg|thumb|280px|right|''The starlit night of [[Lunia]], surrounded by the Silver Sea.'']] Lunia was the location of a number of godly realms, including [[Tyr]]'s secondary realm of [[the Court]].{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|15}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|35}}{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|169}} ===Mercuria=== {{Main|Mercuria}} The second layer, Mercuria was known as the Golden Heaven because a warm golden light suffused everywhere. This layer contained the armory for the noblest warriors who came here for their eternal rest. If necessary, Mercuria was the marshaling ground for the armies of the Heavens. Gentle hills and lush green valleys comprised this layer, which was also dotted with small settlements of archons and other good-aligned beings. Mercuria was known for its great tombs and monuments to noble fighters and paladins resting on the layer. These warriors were honoured during an annual Day of Memory. [[Bahamut]]'s jeweled palace moved about the first four layers of Celestia. It was made entirely from Bahamut's enormous treasure hoard, with walls made of [[mithral]] and windows composed of huge gemstones. Inside, seven great [[wyrm|wyrms]] closely guarded the huge hoard of amassed treasure. ===Venya=== {{Main|Venya}} The third heaven, also called the Pearly Heaven, or Heaven of Pearls, was a lush and verdant land with crops, meadows, moors, hills, and rolling countryside all bathed in the soft glow from a sky reminiscent of the luster of white [[pearl]]s. It was somewhat colder than the previous two layers, its slopes often seen covered with a gentle layer of snow. Peaceful brooks and carefully terraced fields were common on Venya. In the [[Great Wheel cosmology]], the [[halfling pantheon]] made its home in Venya in the realm of [[Green Fields]]. It was a place of safety for the many [[halflings]] that lived there; their crops always gave plentiful harvests and there were no large predators to speak of. ===Solania=== {{Main|Solania}} Solania, the fourth layer, had a sky that glowed like burnished silver and was called the [[Electrum]] Heaven, or sometimes the Crystal Heaven. Its valleys were enveloped in mist, fog, and strange scents. The peaks were home to numerous holy shrines, including monasteries and magnificent cathedrals controlled by [[demigod]]s. Many of the slopes were rich in precious ores and minerals and were mined by populations of dwarves that resided there. Many [[pilgrim]]s came questing to the roof of this layer in the hopes of finding answers to life's persistent questions. In the Great Wheel cosmology, a vast dwarven mansion called [[Erackinor]] was located on the slopes of Solania, where the dwarven deity [[Moradin]] made his domain, with his wife [[Berronar Truesilver]]. It was the location of the giant [[Soul Forges]], which Moradin was said to use to temper the spirits of his people. [[Uroboros]], the Gates of Wisdom, the airborne realm of [[Jazirian]] of the [[couatl]], floated above the mountainside of Solania.{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Mount Celestia|21}}{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Map-Mount Celestia}} ===Mertion=== {{Main|Mertion}} With a sky not too different from Solania's, the fifth layer was known as the [[Platinum]] Heaven. Vast plains and savannas served as the mustering ground for [[paladin]]s and other lawful good servants. Instead of mountains, Mertion had majestic citadels and huge black spherical domes dotting the plains. Access to the next higher layer was found at the tops of the domes.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|87-88}} The city of [[Empyrea]], also known as the City of Tempered Souls, was located on the edge of a cold mountain lake. It was known to host many magical fountains with powerful healing properties, as well as many hospitals and expert healers. ===Jovar=== {{Main|Jovar}} The sixth layer, Jovar, was known as the Glittering Heaven or the Heaven of [[Gem]]s. Its hills were studded with precious gemstones that glittered in the light. This layer was actually a vault lined floor to ceiling with huge [[ruby|rubies]] and [[Garnet (gem)|garnets]] that gave off a glow like a hearth fire. A seemingly unending ziggurat was the home of the Jovarian [[Celestial archon|archons]] and guarded the entrance to the seventh heaven. Known as [[Yesteria]], the Heavenly City, the huge seven-layered ziggurat displayed a large staircase on each face connecting the terraces of each layer. The stones that made up the city were made of precious gemstones, similar to those seen around the surrounding hills. On the topmost terrace was the bridge of [[al-Sihal]], formed of pure light, where the portal to the topmost layer of Celestia, '''Chronias''', was located, It is guarded by a powerful [[solar]] named [[Xerona]] who judged who was allowed to enter. ===Chronias=== {{Main|Chronias}} The topmost and final layer of Celestia, Chronias was called the Illuminated Heaven. Little was known of its structure because nothing was ever recorded by the few who had visited and returned. The legends said that Chronias was so good and lawful that it glowed of its own accord and any who entered had all evil and neutrality burned out of them, leaving them inherently good, if they survived. Many religions made this level the home of their lawful good deities, believing any lesser realms were merely to accommodate less worthy souls. It was thought to be the ultimate goal of the inhabitants of Celestia to ascend the layers one by one in order to reach Chronias, where their souls would join with the essence of the plane itself. ==Inhabitants== [[File:Celestia 4e FRCG.jpg|thumb|230px|The very dramatic slopes of Mount Celestia.]] The [[Celestial archon|archons]]{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|123}} were the native and most numerous inhabitants of the Seven Heavens, cheerfully going about the business of serving the Higher Powers. Many types of archons lived in the first six layers but only rumors existed of a ruling archon ensconced in Chronias. Other creatures found on this plane were [[solar]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|111}} [[planetar]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|101}} [[hollyphant]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|75}} [[deva]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|42}} [[foo creature]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|65}} and [[agathia]].{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|9}} Human and non-human pilgrims, [[shedu]], [[lammasu]], [[ki-rin]], and [[dragon horse]]s{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|59}} would visit fairly often. Collectively, the inhabitants of Celestia were called "'''Celestians'''"."Celestian" is also the name of [[Celestian|a Greyhawk deity]] who owed [[Waukeen]] a favor. She asked him to transport her to the [[Astral Plane]] during the [[Time of Troubles]]. ==Afterlife== {{Main|Afterlife}} The spirits of those who earned a place in the Seven Heavens would become [[lantern archon]]s much the same as evil souls became [[Soul larva|larvae]] in the [[Lower Planes]]. ==Realms== * [[Amaterasu]], sun goddess of the [[Eight Million Gods]], had the realm of [[Radiant Light]] in Mercuria.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|158,179}} * [[Arvoreen]], the patron deity of halfling warriors, made his home in the realm [[Green Fields]] in Venya with the others of his pantheon.{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|115}} * [[Bahamut]] was reported to have realms in Lunia, Mercuria, Venya, and Solania as well as the [[Elemental Plane of Air]]. Whether these were separate realms or [[Bahamut's Palace|one realm]] that moved about, or possibly spanned several layers at once is still a matter of speculation.{{Cite book/Monster Manual 1st edition|33}} * [[Berronar Truesilver]], Mother of Safety, Truth, and Home, lived with her husband Moradin in [[Erackinor|a mountain home]] in Solania.{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|111-112}} * [[Cyrrollalee]], the [[halfling]] deity of friendship and trust, once lived in Green Fields in Venya with the others of her pantheon.{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|116}} * [[Jazirian]], the wise deity of the [[couatl]], has her/his realm [[Uroboros]] hover in the coulds of Solania. * [[Moradin]], the Soul Forger, chief deity of the [[dwarves]], once made his home in Solania within the steep mountains which were called [[Erackinor]] in the dwarven tongue. It was here that Moradin kept the [[Soul Forge]] which he used to temper the spirits and weapons of his people. It was said the smoke from his forge became the mists filling the valleys and the heat from it warmed all of Solania.{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|106}} * [[Torm]] the True maintained his realm of [[Trueheart]] on the layer of Mercuria.{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|162}} * [[Trishina]] maintained no permanent realm, but often wandered Mount Celestia.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|177}}{{Cite book/Monster Mythology|94}} * [[Tyr]] Grimjaws, the Even-Handed, once had a realm called [[the Court]] on the layer of Lunia. * [[Yondalla]], the Protector and Providor of the [[halfling]]s, lead her fellow powers from within the Green Fields in Venya.{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|179}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|111}} ==History== When the multiverse was first created, before any mortals had yet died, Mount Celestia had no archons. The first seven martyrs of law and goodness whose souls arrived from the Material Plane were transformed into the plane's first archons and mandated with the role of ruling its seven layers for eternity. The seven martyrs and their successors continued to rule Celestia as the Celestial Hebdomad.{{Cite book/Book of Exalted Deeds|124}} ==Appendix== ===Notes=== {{Notes}} ===Gallery=== Image:Seven Heavens of Mount Celestia.jpg|''Concept/Promotional art of the 'Seven Heavens of Mount Celestia' made for [[Adventures in the Forgotten Realms]], by [[Alben Tan]].'' ===References=== {{Refs|2}} ===Connections=== {{Mount Celestia}} {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Astral dominions]] [[Category:World Axis planes]] [[Category:Planes of law]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Mountains]] [[Category:Locations on Yggdrasil]]

[[Olympus]] | elevation = {{SI|60000|ft|k}} | georefs = {{Cite book/Tales of the Outer Planes|56}} | races = | socrefs = | usethe = | useon = yes | inhabitants = yes | locations = yes | organizations = yes | settlements = yes | roads = | mountains = | events = yes | food and drink = yes | items = yes }} '''Mount Olympus''' was an enormous cross-planar mountain that connected the [[Prime Material plane]] with the [[Outer Planes]] that were important to the [[Greek pantheon]] via the [[Astral Plane]].{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|45}} ==Description== In the region of [[Arvandor (layer)|Arvandor]] within sight of the mountain, Mount Olympus was the most prominent feature of the landscape, rising above the rest of the plane.{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Adventures in Conflict|5}} It was believed by the [[Fraternity of Order]] that visibility from the mountain's peak could extend as far as {{SI|100|mi|k|long=yes}} in any direction. Travelers claimed that even the other two layers of [[Arborea]], [[Aquallor]] and [[Mithardir]], could sometimes be seen from the summit.{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Travelogue|20}} The slopes of Olympus had a rich landscape of woods and rocky terrain. The southern slope of the mountain was a pastoral region with [[olive]] groves, vineyards, [[apple]] and [[orange]] orchards, and [[sheep]] grazing areas. It was considered the easiest ascent route. Some of the caverns under the mountain were beautiful, filled with colorful [[lichen]] and lit by luminescent rock. The caverns sometimes opened into enormous chambers that defied perception and did not seem at all like an underground environment. Other caverns were damp and small, littered with bones and permeated by rotting smells. ==Cosmography== [[File:Yggdrasil2Hades.jpg|right|thumb|270px|''The planar connections of Mount Olympus (left) and [[Yggdrasil]] (right).'']] The slopes of Mount Olympus were rooted in the [[divine realm]] of [[Olympus]] in the first layer of Arborea. It was the most prominent feature of the realm.{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|50}} At its base, twisting caverns cut through the stone at the veins of the mountain into the [[Lower planes]] of [[Carceri]], [[Gehenna]], and [[Hades]]. Entry points into the planes could be found at round, colored ''[[portal]]s'', in a similar way to the planar connections of [[Yggdrasil]].{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|12}} However, unlike the World Ash, the portals to and from Mount Olympus were well mapped and did not shift over time. Mount Olympus connected to multiple worlds in the [[Prime Material plane]], which were accessible via hidden paths along the mountain. On [[Toril]], the mountain was located on the island of [[Achea]], which lay several hundred miles from [[Faerûn]]. In order to reach Arborea, travelers needed to climb the mountain to the very summit. The Torilian manifestation of Mount Olympus had an elevation of {{SI|60000|ft|k|long=yes}}. The [[World Serpent Inn]] also provided a connection to Mount Olympus and regularly manifested near the slopes of the mountain in Arvandor. Travelers could enter the plane and access the mountain via the inn, but anyone who entered Arborea from the realm of Olympus could only see or access the inn after receiving express authorization from the Greek pantheon. ==Defenses== Although all the ''portals'' leading to and from Mount Olympus were open to anyone trying to cross them, many of the secret paths leading to other planes from the mountain were guarded by creatures in the employ of the Olymian deities. Some of those pahs were only accessible to worshipers of particular deities, while anyone else trying to use them was instead redirected to Hades. ==Inhabitants== Mount Olympus was the home of most deities of the Greek pantheon, who held vast halls and temples on its slopes. The mountain was primarily inhabited by [[nymph]]s, [[satyr]]s, and [[sylph]]s. The caverns of Mount Olympus were inhabited by [[bacchae]], [[oread]]s, and satyrs, among others. ==Rumors & Legends== * A temple of [[Hermes]] that stood within [[Sigil/The Lady's Ward|The Lady's Ward]] of [[Sigil]] was rumored to have a portal that connected the city to Mount Olympus.{{Cite book/In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil|44}} * The entrances to the homes of the Olympian powers were all well disguised. Some believed that this was the doing of [[Hephaestus]], others Hermes, and some believed it was the doing of [[Pan (deity)|Pan]].{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Travelogue|20-21}} ==Appendix== {{Incomplete}} ===Appearances=== :;Adventures ::''[[Tales of the Outer Planes]]'' ::{{Refonly}} ::''[[For Duty & Deity]]'' ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Locations on Toril]] [[Category:Locations on Achea]] [[Category:Locations in Olympus]] [[Category:Locations in Arvandor (layer)]] [[Category:Locations in Arvandor]] [[Category:Locations in the Upper Planes]] [[Category:Locations in Carceri]] [[Category:Locations in Gehenna]] [[Category:Locations in Hades]] [[Category:Locations in the Outer Planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Planar pathways]]

A jagged land of fire and volcanic rock, it was named after the [[divine realm]] of [[Surtr]] that existed within its lands.<ref name="PoCh2e-p123-125" />
==Geography== Muspelheim was formed by similar [[Earthmote|earthberg]]s to those that constituted the first layer, [[Ysgard (layer)|Ysgard]], but they were inverted with respect to those. In Muspelheim, the [[fire]]-lit side faced up, so most of the terrain in the entire layer was dominated by fire and was quite inhospitable to visitors. In many ways, it was very similar to some regions of the [[Elemental Plane of Fire]], which was connected to the layer via numerous portals.<ref name="MotP3e-p90-92" /><ref name="PoCh2e-p123-125" />
==Notable Locations== * [[Muspelheim (realm)|Muspelheim]], realm of [[Surtr]]. It contained some of the few arable lands of the entire layer, which were used to grow [[fireweed]], [[verdobba]], and a type of edible black wood.<ref name="PoCh2e-p123-125" />
==Inhabitants== Since it was such a desolate place, Muspelheim was generally avoided. Only its native [[fire giant]]s remained to care for the land and were its undisputed rulers.<ref name="PoCh2e-p123-125" />

In the wake of the [[Faction War]], the guildmasters and merchant lords fighting over the resulting power vacuum looked as though they might themselves attract the attention of the [[Lady of Pain]]. Three of the most powerful put aside their animosity to form the '''Mutual Trade Association''', or simply the '''Traders'''.
The leaders are:
* {{NPC|Estavan|planar|male|ogre mage|unclassed|5|Fraternity of Order|le}} the Seer, and head of the [[Planar Trade Consortium]] * {{NPC|Shemeshka|planar|female|rakshasa||||ne}} the Marauder * {{NPC|Zadara|planar|female|storm giant|unclassed|20|Merkhants|n}}
Although in theory all three associates share equal power, Shemeshka has emerged as the de facto leader.
The three captains were joined by a number of other influential members in order to take advantage of the organization's benefits. The MTA doesn't interfere with day-to-day affairs, but does look for solutions to common problems affecting everyone: crime waves, disrupted supply lines, worker unrest, and so on.

'''Mystara''' is the primary inhabited world found within [[w:c:spelljammer:Mystaraspace|an unknown crystal sphere]] on the [[Prime Material plane]], and the name of the campaign setting primarily set on this world. It was considered the default setting for the original Dungeons & Dragons game (albeit Basic D&D, not Advanced D&D).
Unusually, the world is hollow, with inner landmasses and an inner sun in place of the planet's core. It's not very involved in planar affairs, but contains its share of interesting magic, particularly in the kingdoms of ''Glantri'' and ''Alphatia''.<ref name="pwhb33">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|page=33}}</ref>
The Hollow World is one of the seven [[Wonders of the Multiverse]]<ref name="poly127-14">{{b|Polyhedron|Polyhedron Magazine 137|page=14}}</ref>

A '''namer''' is someone who is a member of their [[faction]] "in name only" -- they may wear a faction pin in public, attend meetings, offer discounts, and argue philosophy at the local tavern, but they don't fully dedicate themselves to the faction and its beliefs.
Also called "the file" (as in the rank-and-file) or "factioneers," namers typically keep their involvement with their faction to a minimum, and that's typically the way they like it. They can get away with refusing to help, but they'll likewise be unlikely to receive it later. Still, the namers make up the bulk of a faction, so it would be folly to dismiss them.
Namers all typically have their own jobs. If they choose to enlist in the faction full-time, then they become a [[factotum]].

After the [[Spellplague]], the Negative Energy plane collapsed into the [[Elemental Chaos]], mixing with all the other Inner Planes.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|66}} The goddess [[Shar]] managed to channel some of this death energy into the [[Plane of Shadow]] and create the [[Shadowfell]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|69}} Cosmologists believe that [[negative energy]] and its opposite [[positive energy]], combined with the four elements, make up the known universe.{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide v.3.5|148}} This plane was extremely hostile to all forms of life and energy. Only the [[undead]] could travel with impunity here, and the more powerful undead could harness this death energy to attack the living with devastating effect. ==Cosmology== According to the Great Wheel cosmology model, the Negative Energy plane could be reached via the [[Ethereal Plane]] or an adjacent elemental plane, but ''not'' by an elemental vortex. (However, there is speculation that the Void card in the ''[[deck of many things]]'' brought a person here.) If traveling through the Deep Ethereal, a pure black ''curtain of vaporous color'' indicated the boundary of the Plane of Death's Border Ethereal region.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|12}} Such was the influence of the Negative Energy plane that the boundary with the Border Ethereal was weak and fluctuated randomly at times. Travelers thinking they were safe staying in the Border Ethereal could suddenly be dumped on the Plane of Death some distance from the rapidly receding border. Using the [[Great Wheel cosmology#Basic Structure|spherical model]], this plane was adjacent to the quasi-elemental planes of [[Quasielemental Plane of Dust|Dust]], [[Quasielemental Plane of Ash|Ash]], [[Quasielemental Plane of Vacuum|Vacuum]], and [[Quasielemental Plane of Salt|Salt]].{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|52}} Temporary gates could be created by the ''[[plane shift]]'' spell.{{Cite book/Player's Handbook 2nd edition|224}} As described by the World Tree cosmology model, the [[Astral Plane]] connected all planes with the [[Prime Material Plane]] and the Ethereal Plane was only used for journeying between locations on the Prime.{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide v.3.5|147}} The Negative Energy plane was not connected or coterminous with any other elemental plane.{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide v.3.5|150}} The spell ''[[astral projection]]'' {{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide v.3.5|151}}{{Cite book/Player's Handbook v.3.5|201}} could be used to reach the Negative Energy plane via a cold ebony ''color pool''.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|49}} Additionally, the ''[[gate]]'' {{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|33}}{{Cite book/Player's Handbook v.3.5|234}} and ''[[plane shift]]'' {{Cite book/Player's Handbook v.3.5|262}} spells could be used to open a temporary portal to this plane. ==Description== {{quote |It is the blackest night.
It is the heart of darkness.
It is the hunger that devours souls. |[[Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|Manual of the Planes]] }} Both cosmological models described this plane as being an airless, featureless void of darkness with gravity being an individual choice. Somewhat paradoxically, both models also allow that structures existed on a landscape of sorts, either made of the physical, solid darkness, or perhaps of elemental earth that could survive in regions of the plane (called doldrums) that did not exhibit the [[Planar traits#Elemental and Energy Traits|major-negative dominance trait]]. The atmosphere was not vacuum but could not be used by winged creatures for propulsion, nor could it sustain life, yet torches and lanterns would burn for a short while before being extinguished. Magical light sources worked as usual but visibility was extremely limited. These characteristics led cosmologists to speculate that it was the energy-sucking nature of the plane that greedily devoured any life-giving energies rather than the complete lack thereof, but the difference is of interest only to [[sage]]s. In practical terms, without protection from the negative energy and elimination of the need to breathe, death was only a few minutes away at best. Just as there were areas where the negative energy seemed to recede and create the doldrums, some locations exhibited concentrations intense enough to create stable chunks of solid matter that were dubbed [[voidstone]]. These absolutely black blobs ranged from a few inches/centimeters in diameter to the size of a small house and perhaps larger. Anything that touched a voidstone was destroyed in the span of a few heartbeats—even the undead were not immune. This property led scholars to speculate that voidstone may have been a component in the creation of magic items like the ''[[sphere of annihilation]]''. Another curious and deadly property of these silent death traps was that voidstones of a certain size, not too small and not too large, were attracted to life and would move toward the nearest living creature in jerky, uneven leaps. The exact range of this attraction was unknown because of limited visibility, and all reports of attempted mental control indicated failure. ==Inhabitants== The Negative Energy plane was so inimical to life that, in the time of the Great Wheel cosmological model, the only creatures that had actually been seen in the plane were the inscrutable [[outsider]]s, the [[xeg-yi]].{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|128-129}} The "energy vultures" known as [[trilloch]]s were thought to be from this plane but may not have originated here.{{Cite book/Fiend Folio 1st edition|89-90}} By the time the World Tree cosmological model became popular it was discovered that [[undead]] creatures could survive here and that powerful undead, such as [[vampire]]s, [[lich]]es, [[wraith]]s, [[wight]]s, and [[spectre]]s, made this plane their home base. And where undead are found, [[necromancer]]s are seldom far behind. The doldrums were best suited for necromantic work but there was always a danger the negative energy would surge and overwhelm the area. ==Realms== * [[Null]], [[Draconic pantheon|draconic god]] of death, had realms named the [[Mausoleum of Chronepsis]] and the [[Mausoleum of Pain]] in the [[Outlands]] and [[Carceri]], respectively. '''Nephythys''' was an Intermediate Power of the [[Pharaonic pantheon]], the child of [[Geb]] and [[Nut]] and a member of [[Ra]]'s Ennead family.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|84}}</ref> She was [[Set]]'s former wife, but left him after he murdered his brother and rival [[Osiris]]. He never stopped sending proxies to her realm with gifts, but she seemed uninterested, turning the proxies away except for one called Bentresh who she persuaded to serve her rather than her former husband.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|88}}</ref> The goddess was withdrawn to the point of unfriendliness, and didn't receive visitors even from elsewhere in [[Arborea]].<ref>{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|55}}</ref>
Nephythys ruled the realm of [[Amun-thys]] on [[Pelion]], little more than a series of scattered tombs in the layer's massive desert. She and her petitioners guarded their treasure jealously, not out of greed, but just so they didn't get robbed.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|88-89}}</ref>

Each of the nine Hells had its own physical laws or properties of matter, but all were inhospitable or deadly to outsiders. {{Quote |From the boiling rivers of fluid in [[Avernus]] to the sheer crags of [[Nessus]], a body'd be hard-pressed to find a place that sums up the cold cruelty of the multiverse more than Baator does. |[[Nomoto Sinh]], mortal mage.{{Cite book/Faces of Evil: The Fiends|10}} }} ==Cosmology== The [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model placed the Nine Hells in the [[Outer Planes]]{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|73}} between [[Gehenna]] and [[Acheron]], with additional connections to [[Concordant Opposition]] and the [[Astral Plane]].{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|110}} Each Hell was a different infinite layer interconnected at ''barriers'' much like a nine-layered cake—the lowest points of one layer manifested barriers that exited high above the surface of the next lower layer. The river [[Styx]] flowed through the first layer, Avernus, and also the fifth layer, Stygia, before crossing over into Gehenna.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|83}} When the Great Wheel model was overshadowed by the [[World Tree cosmology]] model, the river Styx was renamed the [[River of Blood]] and it flowed through all the [[fiendish planes]] (except for the [[Supreme Throne]] and the [[Demonweb Pits]]) originating in the [[Abyss]], passing through the [[Blood Rift]]—an unusual plane that connected the Abyss with the Nine Hells{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|140}}—bringing the devils even closer to their arch-enemies the [[demon]]s,{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|141}} resulting in the [[Blood War]].{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|142}} The layers were still described as being infinite but with a central pit of finite size that opened to the next lower layer in a tiered fashion, with a drop of many miles between layers. Cosmologists verified portals between the Nine Hells and the [[Barrens of Doom and Despair]] and [[Clangor]] and, by agreement with [[Kelemvor]], to the [[Fugue Plane]].{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|153}} The [[Astral plane]] connected all of the fiendish planes to the [[Prime Material Plane]], but not directly to each other.{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|139}} After the [[Spellplague]], [[Asmodeus]] consumed the essence of the fallen [[Azuth]] achieving (some say regaining) [[Greater deity|greater godhood]] and ended the Blood War by casting the Abyss to the furthest depths of the [[Elemental Chaos]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|73}} The [[World Axis cosmology]] model described the Nine Hells as an [[astral dominion]] floating in the [[Astral Sea]], no longer of infinite size nor consisting of layers, ruled by Asmodeus and his eight [[archdevil]] vassals. Once again the river [[Styx]] flowed through the Nine Hells and the Abyss, but then emptied its pollution into the Astral Sea.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|64,66}} ==Geography== {{/Imagemap}} Each of the Nine Hells was unique and usually mirrored the malevolent characteristics of its ruler, or perhaps the archdevils were shaped by the domains they schemed to control, no one can be certain. In earlier cosmologies, each Hell was a separate infinite layer rigidly joined to its neighbors by barriers at fixed locations.The ''[[Player's Guide to Faerûn]]'' states on page 161 that "the nine layers of this plane are detailed in the ''[[Dungeon Master's Guide 3.5|Dungeon Master's Guide]]'' and ''[[Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|Manual of the Planes]]''" so information about the Nine Hells in those sources should be considered canon when not contradicted by a Forgotten Realms source. After the Spellplague, the domains of the archdevils were described as territories (large, but finite) or circles. The relationships between layers and circles are not fully known. What follows are descriptions of the nine Hells reported for different [[cosmology|cosmological]] models that have been collated and summarized.In other words, the following text merges information from different editions and settings and may originate from conflicting sources. The reader should proceed with caution, as with all things concerning devils. ===Trade=== Inhabitants of the Nine Hells produced goods exported across the planes, including to the planar City of Doors, [[Sigil]]. Green Baator ore and steel smelted from it was mined in Avernus. Another notable export was Baator's own [[whiskey]]. It was a pleasantly-smelling steaming-hot drink that resembled boiling [[goldflow]]. When consumed, it burned one's stomach with sweet pain. Very few mortals could stomach even a single shot.{{Cite game/Planescape: Torment}} ===Avernus=== {{Main|Avernus}} The first circle of Hell was also the "topmost" because Astral travelers would emerge from color pools on this layer and reaching the next circle required descending to the lower depths to breach a barrier to Dis. According to the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model, this layer was also connected by portals to [[Acheron]], [[Gehenna]], and [[Concordant Opposition]]. By the [[World Tree cosmology]] model, portals connected Avernus to [[Clangor]], the [[Barrens of Doom and Despair]] and the [[Blood Rift]] via the [[River of Blood]]. It was believed at the time that some of the archdukes maintained portals to the realms of [[Bane]], [[Loviatar]], and [[Talona]], but the ownership and location of those portals was unknown. The [[World Axis cosmology]] model posits the Nine Hells were isolated with no direct connections except via the river Styx to the [[Abyss]]. Travelers on the [[Astral Sea]] who did not follow the Styx likely found themselves falling out of the sky above Avernus to a fiery death.{{Cite book/Monster Manual 4th edition|61}} [[File:FCII-Avernus-Anne Stokes-p37.jpg|thumb|right|275px|''Avernus, the First Hell.'']] By all accounts Avernus was a desolate wasteland with rocky terrain, sparse, twisted vegetation, concealed snake pits, caves and warrens, volcanoes, and rivers of magma. The sky was starless, full of choking smoke, and glowed a dark red due to balls of flammable gas that floated about or streaked across the atmosphere, randomly exploding as a ''[[fireball]]''.{{Cite dragon/75/The Nine Hells|18}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|116}} During the Blood War, Avernus echoed with the marching of legions of devil troops preparing for the next campaign against the [[demon]]s of the [[Abyss]], the ground was littered with the detritus of countless battles, and blood trickled out of the ground in vein-like streams eventually flowing into the river Styx. ===Dis=== {{Main|Dis}} [[File:FCII-Dis-Warren Mahy-p42.jpg|thumb|right|275px|''Dis, the Second Hell.'']] The second circle of Hell, when described as its own layer, was a flat barren plane containing little more than black, stagnant rivers, stretching for thousands of miles until it reached some rolling hills. The sky was a cloudy dull green shot through with lightning. In the center of this plane rose the Iron City of Dis, several miles in height and hundreds of miles wide. The foul rivers radiated from a moat big enough to be called a lake surrounding the Iron City.{{Cite dragon/75/The Nine Hells|21}} The [[World Tree cosmology|World Tree]] view of the Iron City was much the same but bigger, having been expanded by countless minions following [[Dispater]]'s grand plan. The walls of the buildings and the stones of the streets glowed the dull red of hot iron; more than brief skin contact resulted in severe burns. Prisoners of war, tormented underlings, criminals, and kidnap victims were kept in underground dungeons where their wails of woe could be heard filtering up through small vents in the iron walls. Above it all rose the [[Iron Tower]] where Dispater sat and schemed, untouchable.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|117}} In the [[World Axis cosmology|World Axis]] view, the city of Dis was enclosed in a huge cavern accessible from Avernus through a tremendous iron gate in the side of a mountain. ===Minauros=== {{Main|Minauros}} [[Image:Minauros.jpg|thumb|right|275px|''Minauros, the Third Hell.'']] Minauros as a layer was described as an endless bog of vile pollution, decaying bodies, and rotting marsh, repeatedly drenched by rain, sleet, and hail storms. The soggy, bone-strewn, disease-ridden swampland made movement very difficult and was only broken occasionally by serpentine ridges of volcanic rock.{{Cite dragon/75/The Nine Hells|24}} Nameless creatures even the devils feared inhabited the swamp. Minauros as a realm was depicted as a broad but low-vaulted cavern connected to Dis. An oily water percolated through the roof of the cave and rained down upon swamps, deserts of mud and oozing black soil, pockmarked by bubbling fumaroles and mud geysers. Minauros was also the name of the city built of black stone by [[Mammon]] on the treacherous surface of this place. Only the ceaseless efforts of thousands of minions and slaves prevent the city from sinking and being consumed by the bog. The city of [[Jangling Hiter]], also known as the City of Chains, hung by massive links of chain above the noisome fen and was ruled by [[kyton]]s.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|119}} ===Phlegethos=== {{Main|Phlegethos}} [[File:FCII-Phlegethos-Anne Stokes-p53.jpg|thumb|right|275px|''Phlegethos, the Fourth Hell.'']] The fourth circle was the Hell that most resembled the stereotype of a fiery world of eternal damnation, filled with active volcanoes, rivers of liquid fire, molten rock, ash hills, smoking pits, unbearable heat, all wracked by tremors and earthquakes.{{Cite dragon/75/The Nine Hells|26}} Even the air seemed aflame and thus Phlegethos was considered to be [[Planar traits#Elemental and Energy Traits|fire-dominant]]. In the [[World Axis cosmology|World Axis]] view, Phlegethos was a cavern several miles below Minauros, where burning lava poured out of fissures in the ceiling. The city of Abriymoch was the seat of power in this realm, built of hardened magma, [[obsidian]], and [[Rock crystal|crystal]] in the caldera of an extinct volcano which provided visitors some protection from the elemental environment found throughout the rest of the plane. ===Stygia=== {{Main|Stygia}} [[File:FCII-Stygia-Carl Frank-p56.jpg|thumb|right|275px|''Stygia, the Fifth Hell.'']] The complete opposite of Phlegethos, Stygia was either a bottomless ocean{{Cite book/Stormwrack|9}} covered by an ice sheet up to 3 miles (4.8 kilometers) thick, or a frozen sea salted with huge icebergs buried in a cavern several miles below Dis and hundreds of miles away from fiery Phlegethos depending on which cosmological model was in vogue at the time. According to the [[Great Wheel cosmology|Great Wheel]] and [[World Tree cosmology|World Tree]] models, the river [[Styx]] cut across the ice forming a channel.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|121}} The older model also suggested the Styx supported small but hardy plants and mosses which, after millennia of decay of this vegetation, resulted in swampy areas along the banks of the river. A few floating islands were the only non-frozen ground in Stygia, their peaks wreathed in lightning arcing from the coal-black sky. Where lightning struck, a strange phenomenon called "cold fire" erupted: white flames of extreme cold that "burned" for a short time and then disappeared without a trace.{{Cite dragon/75/The Nine Hells|30}} The great city of [[Tantlin]] was built upon one of these islands, in the curve of the swampy Styx, or perhaps on a giant ice floe. Due to the proximity of the Styx, Tantlin was a cross-planar trading post for those brave enough to attempt navigating the treacherous river. {{Cite book/Stormwrack|9}} ===Malbolge=== {{Main|Malbolge}} [[File:FCII-Malbolge-Tom Baxa-p61.jpg|thumb|right|275px|''Malbolge, the Sixth Hell.'']] There is significant disagreement between cosmologies on the nature of the sixth circle of Hell. As a Great Wheel layer, Malbolge was a gargantuan tumble of angular black stone blocks, each block ranging in size from a small city to a large metropolis, that formed a pile hundreds of miles thick. The randomly tilted and ill-fitting blocks were honeycombed with angular passages and caverns causing non-flying travelers to frequently need mountaineering skills and risk avalanches. Stinking clouds of vapor rose up from the depths and lit the sky with the color of blood, causing cosmologists to speculate that the blocks of Malbolge may have rested on an infinite sea of lava. Corroborating reports have been heard of flammable materials left on the ground spontaneously combusting.{{Cite dragon/76/The Nine Hells, Part II|22}} Most habitations in Malbolge were copper-clad fortresses built from black stone. The World Tree view of this layer was similar to the Great Wheel plane of [[Gehenna]]: a steep, infinite craggy incline often subject to avalanches that crushed most anything that got in the way. The copper-shod redoubts were teardrop-shaped or otherwise engineered to deflect tumbling boulders, but even those could not long withstand a direct hit from a major avalanche. In the [[World Axis cosmology]] view, Malbolge was another huge cavern connected to Stygia by icy canals that ran hundreds of miles before reaching their destination. A former godly inhabitant had shaped the realm into a vast garden with fountains, towers, reflecting pools, and all manner of landscaping delights. With the coming of the devils, Malbolge was still beautiful on the surface but creeping corruption permeated the realm, twisting the beauty, perverting the architecture, and poisoning the pools. ===Maladomini=== {{Main|Maladomini}} [[File:FCII-Maladomini-Eric Deschamps-p66.jpg|thumb|right|275px|''Maladomini, the Seventh Hell.'']] The [[Great Wheel cosmology]] view of the seventh circle of Hell described it as having vapor-polluted skies similar to Malbolge but the surface was solid. The post-Spellplague view described Maladomini as a colossal maze of passages each several miles across that eventually led to Cania, Malbolge, and Nessus. All three models agreed that the seventh Hell was filled with ruins of old cities, stagnant rivers, exhausted and abandoned quarries and strip mines, stone aqueducts and lava canals, decaying fortresses, swarms of biting flies, and black pools of ichor that erupted from the ground. The Lord of the Seventh was never satisfied with the construction of his capitol and repeatedly built and abandoned city after city. The largest and most beautiful was Malagard, a sprawling metropolis/palace/fortress/arcology with myriad black towers linked by a tangled web of bridges and walkways. Malagard was rumored to contain a million rooms and to cap an equally complex dungeon labyrinth.{{Cite dragon/76/The Nine Hells, Part II|24}} ===Cania=== {{Main|Cania}} [[File:FCII-Cania-Anne Stokes-p69.jpg|thumb|right|275px|''Cania, the Eighth Hell.'']] Both pre- and post-Spellplague cosmologies agree that CaniaThe ''[[Manual of the Planes 1st edition]]'' (page 109) and ''[[Dragon_(magazine)|Dragon #76]]'' (page 26) spelled the name of the eighth layer "Caina" but ''[[Manual of the Planes 3rd edition]]'' (page 122) and ''[[Monster Manual 4th edition]]'' (page 61) corrected it to "Cania". was a bitterly [[Planar traits#Elemental and Energy Traits|cold-dominant]] realm of solid ice mountains, titanic, unnaturally fast-moving glaciers, and nearly continuous snowfall that made Stygia seem balmy by comparison. Unprotected travelers were exposed to temperatures of −60{{degreesF}} (−51{{degreesC}}) but on the positive side there were few creatures that hunted in the icy wastes. Earlier lore described the great citadel Mephistar as being constructed of iron{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|111}}{{Cite dragon/76/The Nine Hells, Part II|28}} but later reports say the Lord of the Eighth's fortress/palace was made of ice.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|122}} All accounts seemed to agree the tower had a heated, luxurious interior and sat atop a gargantuan glacier called Nargus whose speed and movement were under the control of [[Mephistopheles]] himself. ===Nessus=== {{Main|Nessus}} [[File:Nessus.jpg|thumb|right|200px|''Nessus, the Ninth Hell.'']] The ninth and deepest Hell was a land of extremes in the [[Great Wheel]] view: regions cold as Cania, volcanoes like Phlegethos, a lake of ice, a flaming forest, sheer cliffs, ''firewinds'',{{Cite dragon/76/The Nine Hells, Part II|32-34}} and a citadel even larger than [[Khin-Oin]] in [[Hades]] (later, the Khin-Oin became part of the [[Abyss]]{{Cite book/Demonomicon|51}}). The [[World Tree cosmology|World Tree]] view did not contradict this description of Nessus but focused more on the blasted and torn landscape out of which rose Malsheem, the Citadel of Hell. It was said that Malsheem could hold millions of devils within its mountainous edifice, from the lowest warrens deep in the trench to the soaring spires miles above the tortured plane.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|123}} The [[World Axis cosmology|World Axis]] model agreed that a progression of rifts, pits, and chasms lead down and down, forming a vertical maze hundreds of miles deep that contained great cities, fiendish armies, and the mighty fortress of the Overlord [[Asmodeus]]. ==Inhabitants== {{main|Devil}} The principal inhabitants of the Nine Hells/Baator were the [[devil]]s,{{Cite book/Monster Manual 1st edition|20}}{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|44}}{{Cite book/Monster Manual 4th edition|60}} and their offspring{{Cite book/Monster Manual 4th edition|39}} in varieties too numerous to catalog here. See the main article for descriptions of the myriad devilkind. Unlike the [[demon]]s of the [[Abyss]], the devils were highly organized in their quest for power and status—scheming and plotting power plays, coups, and assassinations. In addition to the devils, this plane was home to [[bonespear]]s, [[gathra]], [[haraknin]], [[hell hound]]s, [[imp]]s, [[night hag]]s, [[nightmare]]s, and [[maelephant]]s. Also occasionally encountered were [[achaierai]], [[barghest]]s, [[hellcat]]s, [[mephit]]s, [[rakshasa]], and [[stench kow]]s.{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|45}} ==Afterlife== {{Main|Afterlife}} Beliefs about the journey of souls to the afterlife changed with the shifting [[cosmology|cosmologies]] and the [[crystal sphere]] in which one resided. In some worlds, [[lawful evil]] souls were automatically destined for the Hells and arrived as mindless [[nupperibo]]s{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|49}} or, if they were worthy, as semi-intelligent [[lemure]]s.{{Cite book/Monster Manual 1st edition|23}} For mortals of [[Realmspace]], however, souls first traveled to the [[Fugue Plane]] where they awaited escort to their final rest on the plane of their primary deity.{{Cite book/Faiths and Avatars|2-3}} While waiting, devils were allowed to bargain with the souls, playing on their fears and doubts to get them to agree that becoming a lemure with a chance for promotion was a better option than their suspected fate. Strong or crafty souls might negotiate a deal that reduced their time as a lemure or bestow a boon or punishment on those they left behind.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|259}} After the [[Spellplague]], [[Shar]] reshaped the [[Plane of Shadow]] and folded in what death energy did not get absorbed into the [[Elemental Chaos]] and created the [[Shadowfell]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|69}} According to the [[World Axis cosmology|World Axis]] view, souls on their way to the afterlife started their journey in the Shadowfell. Most made it to the Fugue Plane to await judgment, but a few remained behind or were lost.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|65}} ==Realms== [[File:The Abyss.jpg|thumb|right|400px|''Asmodeus and his armies attacking demons in the Blood War.'']] The nine circles of Hell were each ruled by an [[archdevil]] of great power, but the Nine Hells were also the home of other powerful beings at various points in the history of the Realms. Listed here in alphabetical order are those that directly or indirectly influenced the course of events in [[Faerûn]], [[Toril]], and beyond. * [[Asmodeus]], the Overlord of the Nine Hells, exercised his power from a gargantuan citadel in the lowest rift of Nessus, named ''Malsheem''. * [[Azharul]]'s [[Dragonspawn Pits]] were located in Avernus. * [[Baalzebul]] ruled the seventh circle of Hell, Maladomini, from his huge fortress ''Malagard''. Early source material credited Baalzebul as controlling the sixth circle (Malbolge){{Cite book/Monster Manual 1st edition|21}} through his viceroy [[Moloch]].{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|48}} * [[Bahgtru]], the strong but dim-witted son of [[Gruumsh]], once resided in the Nine Hells{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|119}} before moving to the [[astral dominion]] of [[Nishrek]] as described by the [[World Tree cosmology|World Tree]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|162}} and [[World Axis cosmology|World Axis]] cosmology models. * [[Belial]] was the ruler of Phlegethos, the fourth circle of Hell,{{Cite book/Monster Manual II (1983)|46}} based in the basalt palace ''Abriymoch'' the "Mount of Leaping Flames", nestled in the caldera of an extinct volcano. Sometime before the [[Spellplague]] he set his daughter [[Fierna]] up as the ostensible ruler while he directed from the wings. * [[Dispater]] dominated the second circle of Hell, Dis, from his high stone (later iron) tower in the city of the same name, also called the ''Iron City''. * [[Fierna]], daughter of [[Belial]], was the archduchess of the fourth circle, fiery Phlegethos, as much as her father allowed. * [[Gargauth]] was thought to have been an [[archdevil]] cast out of the Hells long ago for betrayal. Mildly [[chaos]]-aligned{{Cite dragon/291/Sage Advice|108}} | magical-WT = | faith-WT = Strong faith trait | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = {{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|257}}{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|140}} | inhabitants = yes | deities = yes | locations = yes | organizations = yes | settlements = yes | usethe = | useon = }} '''Nishrek''' was a [[fiendish plane]] in the [[World Tree cosmology]] model and later an [[astral dominion]] in the [[World Axis cosmology]] model. Prior to the discovery of the [[World Tree]], it was [[Gruumsh]]'s realm in [[Acheron]], occupying one face of a gigantic cube{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|133}} (and then later, the whole cube{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|124}}{{Cite book/Complete Divine|128}}) as described by the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model. Nishrek was the last known home of the [[orc pantheon]],{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|125}}{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|161}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Player's Guide|159}}{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|16}} which tended to wander or be forced out of various previous homes.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|114}} ==Description== Nishrek was once just the name of Gruumsh's realm, stuck to the side of a moon-sized cube floating in the air of Acheron. As new [[cosmology|cosmologies]] were invented to explain what planar travelers discovered, the name followed Gruumsh to new realms and became synonymous with the plane he dominated. Endless war was a constant across all cosmological models,{{Cite book/The Planewalker's Handbook|15}} made possible by the positive-dominant feature of this plane—all those who died in battle were raised at sunset to fight again the next night.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|113}} ===Great Wheel Model=== As a realm in Acheron, Nishrek was a square, flat, barren plain broken only by trenches dug for defense, conical pits and mountains, perhaps a segment of the River [[Styx]], and the occasional iron citadel, which the orcs and other evil races merely occupied until the tide of battle pushed or pulled them elsewhere. The main conflicts were between the orcs and the [[goblin]]s, but there was plenty of inter-tribe squabbling as well. ===World Tree Model=== When the World Tree cosmology supplanted the Great Wheel model, Nishrek became its own plane, which the orcs had all to themselves, but without much improvement in the environment, although there was at least a sea and some hills.{{Cite web/Manual of the Planes: Frequently Asked Questions|3}} The Manual of the Planes FAQ states that Nishrek was "similar to the first layer of Ysgard, but dangerous and evil." The entry on page 91 of the ''[[Manual of the Planes 3rd edition]]'' describes Ysgard as "rough and wild" with "hilly terrain leading down to cold seas." It was an immeasurable plane with battlements, entrenchments, and fortresses, contested over nightly by petitioners who healed quickly and even regenerated lost limbs. If they fell in battle, they received a ''[[true resurrection]]'' at the next sunset and joined the battle again. Each tribe vied for the favor of Gruumsh, whom they believed would someday declare a winner and thereby raise the status of their tribe above all others. ===World Axis Model=== When the [[Spellplague]] caused Nishrek to be cast adrift upon the [[Astral Sea]], it changed from being a practically limitless plain to a finite [[dominion]] with a more varied landscape—dense forests, broiling deserts, flinty badlands, murky rivers and foreboding seas—all bearing the ravages of constant war. Like [[Warrior's Rest]], this plane tallied untold deaths but no losses, as each combatant rose to fight again and again. ==Inhabitants== The only creatures tenacious enough to call Nishrek home were swarms of [[Hellwasp swarm|hellwasps]], which could ruin the best-laid battle plans very quickly. [[Rust dragon]]s were also seen on this plane, as well as [[styx dragon]]s where the [[River of Blood]] ran its course. Orc and [[half-orc]] (including [[orog]] and [[tanarukk]]{{Cite book/Faiths & Pantheons|149}}) petitioners made up the vast majority of the population, organized by tribe and faction. After the Spellplague, [[ogres]] and [[troll]]s saw Nishrek in the [[afterlife]], when [[Vaprak]] became an [[exarch]] of Gruumsh. ==Realms== * [[Bahgtru]] the Leg Breaker{{Cite book/Faiths & Pantheons|148}} made his home in Gruumsh's [[Iron Fortress]]. Prior to this, his home was one of the smaller cubes that floated in orbit around the moon-sized block that held Nishrek in [[Acheron]]. * [[Gruumsh]] the One-Eyed God was the primary power that shaped Nishrek and built his Iron Fortress large enough to hold armies (when he deigned to allow them in). * [[Ilneval]] the Hoard Leader's fate after the Spellplague was unknown. Prior to his disappearance, he shared the Iron Fortress with Gruumsh and Bahgtru. During his time on Acheron, he also had a geometrically shaped satellite. * [[Luthic]] the Cave Mother{{Cite book/Faiths & Pantheons|150}} carved her lair out of solid rock and iron with her incredibly long claws{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|120–121}} deep beneath the Iron Fortress. * [[Obould]] was once [[King Obould Many-Arrows]] in Faerûn until he became an exarch of Gruumsh and joined the orcish pantheon in the Iron Fortress. * [[Shargaas]] the Stalker Below carved out a pitch-black realm somewhere deep under the surface of Nishrek. Prior to this, his realm, known as the [[Night Below]], was located in the coldest, darkest layer of [[Gehenna]].{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|134}}{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|119}} * [[Vaprak]], god of ogres and trolls,{{Cite book/Faiths & Pantheons|221}} also made his home in caverns somewhere on this plane after he became an exarch of Gruumsh. He moved here after the Spellplague from Shatterstone, the 524th [[Layers of the Abyss|layer]] of the [[Abyss]].{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|176}}{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|111}} * [[Yurtrus]] White Hands{{Cite book/Faiths & Pantheons|151}} had a towering hill named [[Fleshslough]] overlooking the battlefields of Nishrek, where the threat of permanent death by unimaginably horrible means was enough to motivate most petitioners to give their best effort in battle. Before joining the rest of the orc pantheon in Nishrek, he made his home in the Gray Wastes of [[Hades]].{{Cite book/Unearthed Arcana 1st edition|120}} ==Appendix== ===Notes=== {{Notes}} ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Acheron}} {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Astral dominions]] [[Category:Divine realms]] [[Category:Fiendish planes]] [[Category:World Tree planes]] [[Category:World Axis planes]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Locations in Acheron]] [[Category:Locations in the Outer Planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Locations on the River Styx]] [[Category:Locations in the Lower Planes]]

{{Creature | image = <gallery> Modrnona.gif|2e Nonaton1e.jpg|1e </gallery> | caption = A nonaton. | name = Nonaton | size5e = | type5e = | subtype5e = | alignment5e = | challenge5e = | refs5e = | size4e = Large | origin4e = [[Immortal]] | type4e = [[Animate]] | subtype4e = [[Modron]] | alignment4e = | refs4e = <ref name="D414-Ecology-p15">{{Cite dragon/414/Ecology of the Modron|15}}</ref> | size3e = Large | type3e = [[Outsider]] | subtype3e = | alignment3e = Always [[lawful neutral]] | challenge3e = 10 | refs3e = <ref name="WEM3e-p11-12">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition/WE1|11-12}}</ref> | size2e = Large | alignment2e = [[Lawful neutral]] | refs2e = <ref name="PCS-MS2e-p16-18,20">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/Monstrous Supplement|16-18,20}}</ref> | size1e = | alignment1e = [[Lawful neutral]] | refs1e = <ref name="MMII1e-89">{{Cite book/Monster Manual II 1st edition|89}}</ref> | patron deity =[[Primus]] | vision = [[Darkvision]], [[Blindsight]]<ref name="WEM3e-p11-12" /><ref name="D414-Ecology-p15" /> | activecycle = | diet = | lifespan = | location = | language = [[Celestial language|Celestial]], [[Modron language|Modron]], [[Infernal language|Infernal]]<ref name="WEM3e-p11-12" /> | subraces = | climate = Any<ref name="WEM3e-p11-12" /> | terrain = Any land<ref name="WEM3e-p11-12" /> | height = | length = | wingspan = | weight = | skincolor = | haircolor = | hairstyles = | feathers = | eyecolor = | build = | distinctions = | based = | first = [[Monster Manual II 1st edition|''Monster Manual II'' 1{{st}} edition]] }} '''Nonatons''' were the second-lowest rank of hierarch [[modron]]s in the modron hierarchy.<ref name="MMII1e-89" />
==Description== A nonatons body was shaped like a cylinder. A ring of nine tentacles circled its midriff, an equal distance from one another. Two stout legs provided locomotion. On each side of of the upper part of its body, it had two eyes and mouths on opposite sides.<ref name="WEM3e-p11-12" />
==Combat== If forced into combat, a nonaton used a combination of psionics, spells and their tentacles.<ref name="WEM3e-p11-12" />
==Abilities== Like all hierarch modrons, nonatons had the innate ability to duplicate the effects of ''[[clairaudience]]'', ''[[clairvoyance]]'', ''[[command]]'', ''[[dimension door]]'', ''[[teleport without error]]'', and ''[[wall of force]]'' spells at will.<ref name="TGMMp126">{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|126}}</ref> Additionally, they were able to duplicate the effects of ''[[detect charm]]'', ''[[detect evil and good]]'', ''[[detect lie]]'', ''[[ESP]]'', ''[[mirror image]]'', ''[[slow]]'' and ''[[web]]'' spells at will. Once per day, a nonaton could cast ''[[power word, stun]]''.<ref name="TGMMp127">{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|127}}</ref> Nonatons were immune to effects and spells that influenced the mind and had a resistance to acid, cold and fire.<ref name="WEM3e-p11-12" />
==Society== There were exactly 81 nonatons in modron society. They acted as captains and chief inspectors of the [[pentadrone]] police force. One served each sector, nine served the [[tertian]]s, and the remaining eight reported directly to [[Primus]] himself. Each nonaton had twelve pentadrone lieutenants, each of whom commanded twelve [[quadrone]] sergeants, who in turn each commanded twelve [[tridrone]]s.<ref name="MMII1e-89" />
Nonatons are often used to head investigations into [[rogue modron]]s.
==Ecology== Nonatons were able to see in all directions simultaneously, due to the placement of their two eyes. They were able to see in [[darkvision]] up to {{SI|60|ft}}. They could communicate to any sentient creature within {{SI|63|mi|k}} telepathically.<ref name="WEM3e-p11-12" />

==Description== Unlike most quadrones, Nordom had a second pair of arms instead of wings.<ref name="PST" />
==Possessions== Nordom wielded a pair of [[gear spirit]]s that were shaped and functioned like [[crossbow]]s.<ref name="PST" />

After the march, Nordom remained in Waterdeep, even taking part in a mission to protect one of the [[Lords of Waterdeep]] from an assassination attempt. Due to his resemblance to his non-rogue kin, he was unpopular with Waterdhavians affected by the march.<ref name="ICotFR" />

'''Now in Print''' is the print-on-demand (PoD) program operated by Wolves of Freeports's series of sites: DMsGuild, DriveThruRPG, DriveThruComics, and DriveThruFiction. The program converts D&D's back catalog to a print format wherever possible through the use of original electronic files or high-resolutio nscans.
Many older products are out of print and no longer supported; the secondary market prices for some of these older books can be astronomical. The Now in Print program means they'll never be out of print again.

'''Nut''' was an Intermediate Power of the [[Pharaonic pantheon]], the daughter of [[Shu]] and [[Tefnut]] and a member of [[Ra]]'s Ennead family.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|84}}</ref> Her love with her brother-husband [[Geb]] was forbidden by Ra and Shu, and they were kept apart by the latter's atmosphere domain.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|91}}</ref>
Nut ruled the realm of [[the Refuge of Night]] on [[Belierin]], a directionless field of starry sky where petitioners manifested as the stars themselves. Although she knew she wasn't beyond Ra's reach, she enjoyed the layer's solitude.<ref>{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|90}}</ref>

{{Body of water | image = Oceanus_dragon-3e.jpg | caption = An Oceanus dragon protecting travelers from a storm on the River Oceanus. | name = River Oceanus | aliases = | type = River | region = [[Outer Planes]] | size = | depth = | river source = [[Thalasia]] | river mouth = [[Aquallor]] | tributaries = | tributary of = | georefs = <ref name="MotP3e-p21,77,86,138-146">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|21,77,86,138-146}}</ref> | races = | socrefs = | usethe = yes | useon = yes | inhabitants = yes | locations = yes | organizations = | settlements = | mountains = | events = | food and drink = | items = | based = [[wikipedia:en:Oceanus|Oceanus]] (Greek) }} The '''Oceanus''' was a river that connected several [[upper planes]] of the [[Great Wheel cosmology]].<ref name="MotP3e-p21,77,86,138-146" />
==Geography== The Oceanus's source was located in [[Thalasia]], the fourth layer of [[Elysium]]. From there, it flowed through the layers of [[Belierin]], [[Eronia]], and [[Amoria]], moving on to [[Krigala]], the first layer of the [[Beastlands (plane)|Beastlands]], where it was joined by several streams flowing from the second layer, [[Brux]]. Finally, the river passed through [[Arvandor (layer)|Arvandor]] and ended by flowing into the waters of [[Aquallor]], the second layer of [[Arborea]], although several maelstroms at the bottom of the infinite ocean transported travelers back to the river's headwaters in Thalasia. This cyclic nature led many sages to believe that the Oceanus, in fact, had no beginning and no end.<ref name="MotP3e-p21,77,86,138-146" /><ref name="PoC-BoC2e-p50">{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|50}}</ref>
Close to Arborea, the river was tenuously drawn to the [[Gates of the Moon]] in [[Ysgard (layer)|the first layer]] of [[Ysgard]]. The connection, however, was faint, and dependent on the tides.<ref name="PC-BC2e-p107">{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|107}}</ref>
The water of the Oceanus was sweet and fragrant.<ref name="MotP3e-p21,77,86,138-146" /> Its banks were broad, its surface was calm, and its depth was immeasurably great. Travel time along the Oceanus varied, as the borders between [[planes]] were not always objectively located.<ref name="PCS-DM2e-p44">{{Cite book/Planescape Campaign Setting/A DM Guide to the Planes|44}}</ref>
[[File:DMG5e_-_Elysium_-_Olly_lawson_-_p60.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''The plane of Elysium along the banks of the Oceanus.'']] The Oceanus dominated the features of all four layers of Elysium. The river branched off and rejoined throughout its flow, sometimes even doubling back on itself at certain places.<ref name="MotP1e-p90">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|90}}</ref>
The river was the main means of travel throughout the layers of Elysium, and was frequently used to connect to the other planes along its course. Although the river did not suffer from pirate raids, there were many natural hazards along its course, such as rapids, eddies, and whirlpools, as well as large natural predators.<ref name="PoConf-LB2e-p52">{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|52}}</ref>
Many towns were established along the banks of the Oceanus. Its course was always populated with boats sailing up or downstream. It was easy to rent or hire boats in one such town.<ref name="PCS-DM2e-p44" />
==History== The Oceanus was the preferred course of the [[Great Modron March]] as it passed through Amoria towards the [[gate-town]] of [[Ecstasy]] in the [[Outlands]].<ref name="GMM2e-p42">{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|42}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== The River Oceanus was guarded by [[Oceanus dragon]]s, who protected travelers along its course from evil creatures and natural hazards.<ref name="DN3e-p181-182">{{Cite book/Draconomicon: The Book of Dragons|181-182}}</ref> Although they spent most of the time on patrol, it was common for Oceanus dragons to visit the [[Dragon Eyrie]] from time to time.<ref name="PGF3e-p150">{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|150}}</ref>
The depths of the river were also inhabited by [[delphon]]s, or songsharks, mysterious singing creatures that could reveal secrets about the Oceanus itself or the workings of the [[multiverse]] to careful listeners.<ref name="PoConf-MS2e-p8">{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Monstrous Supplement|8-9}}</ref> Other intelligent aquatic life that could be found in its waters included [[asrai]], [[balaena]],<ref>{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|6,52}}</ref> [[dolphin]]s, [[nereid]]s, [[selkie]]s, and [[aquatic elves]].<ref>{{Cite book/Planes of Conflict/Liber Benevolentiae|52}}</ref>

==Description== Octons looked like an elongated cylinder that tapered to a point at the top. Just below this point and on either side they had a set of two eyes and a mouth. About a third of the way down their body was a collar-like "shoulder" ring that encircled their entire body. Attached to this ring were eight evenly-spaced tentacles.<ref name="MotPWE3e" />
==Combat== If forced into combat, an octon used a combination of innate abilities, spells and their tentacles.<ref name="MotPWE3e" />
==Abilities== Like all hierarch modrons, octons had the innate ability to duplicate the effects of ''[[clairaudience]]'', ''[[clairvoyance]]'', ''[[command]]'', ''[[dimension door]]'', ''[[haste]]'', ''[[telekinesis]]'', ''[[teleport without error]]'', and ''[[wall of force]]'' spells at will.<ref name="TGMM-p126">{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|126}}</ref> Additionally, they were able to duplicate the effects of ''[[detect evil and good]]'', ''[[haste]]'', ''[[telekinesis]]'' and ''[[water walk]]'' spells. Octons were able to cast [[divine]] spells from the [[Law domain|Law]], [[Protection domain|Protection]] and [[War domain|War]] domains. Octons were immune to all effects that influenced the mind and all psionic-based attacks and had a resistance to acid, cold and fire.<ref name="MotPWE3e" /><ref name="TGMM-p127">{{Cite book/The Great Modron March|127}}</ref>
==Society== There were exactly 64 octons in modron society. They acted as governors to each of the sixty-four sectors of [[Nirvana]]. As such, they were considered responsible for the base modrons of their sector, as well as the [[decaton]]s and [[nonaton]]s that were assigned to them. Each octon had a personal staff consisting of one decaton, one nonaton, five [[pentadrone]]s, sixteen [[quadrone]]s, eighty-one [[tridrone]]s, two hundred and fifty-six [[duodrone]]s, and one thousand, seven hundred and twenty eight [[monodrone]]s. They maintained small towers, which resembled smaller versions of the towers of the [[quarton]]s, the [[Secundus|secundi]], and [[Primus]].<ref name="MMII1e-89">{{Cite book/Monster Manual II 1st edition|89}}</ref>
==Ecology== Octons were able to float through air and water with equal ease. Locomotion was provided by forcing either air or water through its collar-like shoulder ring. Due to the position of their eyes, octons had a 360 degree field of vision and could see in [[darkvision]] up to {{SI|60|ft}}. Octons were able to communicate telepathically with any sentient creature within {{SI|80|mi|k}}.<ref name="MotPWE3e" />

'''Oerth''' is the primary inhabited world found within [[w:c:spelljammer:Greyspace|Greyspace]] on the [[Prime Material plane]]. Contrary to most other Prime systems, it's geocentric, with Oerth at the center, orbited by the sun, Liga. Although not as magic-rich as worlds like [[Toril]], some of the most well-known sorcerers of the planes come from this world.
Oerth is most infamous as the home of the lich-turned-power, [[Vecna]].

'''Ortho''' the homeworld of the [[Harmonium]] faction on the [[Prime Material plane]].
The Harmonium began in [[374 BFHR]] as an adventuring party on the Prime world of Ortho, setting a goal to "rid the country of chaos and bring peace to the land." Unlike most such parties, they actually did it. Gradually, they would bring peace to the entire world (whether it wanted it or not). Occasionally chaos would rampage across the land, and they tracked these to demonic incursions from the [[Outer Planes]]. <ref name="fm90">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17275|page=90}}</ref> Once they discovered the Outer Planes, it wasn't long before they found their way to [[Sigil]].<ref name="pwhb33">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|page=33}}</ref>
